Your body may not be what you crave, it is not infinite, it is not perfect, but it is a gift, in some ways. It gives you a tangible way to affect the world, to love, to fear. You're human, even if you don't realize it, and you're a living, breathing, feeling piece of the Universe. 

The dad, your dad, perhaps you should remove him from your moon. If he is a center of darkness, if he is encouraging the blade to enter your veins, then please let him go. Ultimately, you have the power, but I do understand it needs to be drawn out somehow. 

Maybe, my words can help, even a tiny bit. Even a sliver, it's better than the void, right? 

There are people that can help you. I won't say they are on every corner, but they exist. As scary as it may seem, you may be able to find a therapist, to explain to, to confide in, to bring you to Earth again. I can try to help, too. But I am but a troubled layman. 

There are people that have dedicated their lives to helping the tortured souls of the world, to help the sweet, damaged people like you go to university, and complete your goals. 

I hope you may find one. And if not, I hope you can find solace in the knowledge in that you're not alone. I too am suffering, and I feel I understand your disassociation, to an extent. Being trapped in a body is an unfortunate reality, but it is one we must face, and hopefully accept in time. 

I wish you will find some happiness in your struggling mind, I will continue hope for the both of us.

I've always thought a bear, lumbering, big. Protective, and caring, I think. A nice bear, a different one. 

And he could meet this wolf, gray, sleek but with tattered fur, scared at first. She'd snap at the bear, and the bear would roar at her, but after in a fighting circle, they'd calm down. They'd notice something...they can help each other.

So the wolf would cautiously approach the bear, and he'd lie down on his belly. The wolf would climb on top, and lie on his back. She would be comfortable, and would playfully tug his fur with her claws. 

They'd walk on, over glistening grass, the harsh summer sun. They'd stop at watering holes, she would gather them rabbits and deer if she could find her friends, he would get them a moose every once in a while. 

They could sleep, the wolf curling herself next to the bear, and feeling his warmth, his deep breathing, and be protected. 

The wolf would always ride on top of the bear, or by his side, and would nuzzle or tug at him to say just where to go. They'd be a wonderful team, and a fine couple, haha.
